title: Sonatina in C major, Op. 36 No. 1 (1st movement, exposition)
subtitle: Spiritoso - exposition only, repeat not taken
trains: A brisk single-line melody in the right hand (scale runs, octave leaps, a brief secondary-dominant tonicization) over a light, mostly on-the-beat left hand - reading fluency and a fast, even tempo more than technical difficulty.
limitations: tempo lowered to 144 to fit level (source's 156 is editorial)

provenance.author: Musicanyya practice material
provenance.basedOn: Muzio Clementi, Sonatina in C major, Op. 36 No. 1 (published 1797, public domain; Clementi died 1832), 1st movement (Spiritoso). Pitches and rhythm for measures 1-15 (both hands) were transcribed and checked note-by-note against the Mutopia Project's public-domain LilyPond engraving (piece-info id 804, sonatina-1.ly, after the G. Schirmer 1893 Sonatina Album edition), including cross-checking the relative-octave arithmetic against the piece's well-known melodic contour and against the internal harmonic/voice-leading consistency of the reconstructed left hand.
provenance.note: Exposition only (the source's own measures 1-15, up to its written repeat sign), played once; the notated repeat back to measure 1, and the movement's development/recapitulation (measures 16-38 of the source), are not included. The 'Spiritoso' marking is Clementi's, but the metronome mark is the Schirmer editor's; it was lowered from 156 to 144 for this file so it sits inside this level's tempo cap while keeping the 'Spiritoso' character.
